title: Holistic quality pipeline for quant profile validation and gating
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: As we onboard FP8/INT8 quantization profiles into the serving runtime, we need a reproducible, performant quality evaluation pipeline that provides per-profile and per-model quality signals (token-level and task-level) and enforces gating rules during rollouts. Existing eval tooling is fragmented across research notebooks and the eval harness; we lack a unified metric contract, lightweight scorers suitable for CI, and an orchestration layer that ties calibration outputs to pass/fail decisions for rollouts.

Proposal: Implement a Holistic Quality Pipeline (HQP) that: (1) provides standardized metric contracts for perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, ROUGE/BLEU, F1/EM for QA, and a registry for task-specific scorers; (2) offers both distributed and single-node fast scorers optimized for calibration runs (tokenization and metric caching, batched scoring, optional GPU acceleration); (3) integrates with the calibration workflow to emit per-profile delta reports and gating decisions (A/B and canary); (4) exposes results to Console (per-profile dashboards) and to CI/CD for automated gating; (5) includes reproducible config, seeds, and dataset manifests so results are comparable across commits and environments.

Key design decisions: standardized tokenization/normalization policy (shared tokenizers and detokenizers for generation metrics), separate "reference ingestion" contracts for task datasets (MMLU, Summarization sets, QA gold sets), and a modular scorer API (Python + Rust bindings) so we can run lightweight checks in CI and heavy validations offline. The pipeline should produce a canonical JSON artifact for each run that includes metric vectors (per-task/per-example), aggregated summaries, confidence intervals, and metadata (model, quant-profile, seed, dataset commit).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable scorer registry implemented with pluggable adapters for: perplexity (token-level, NLL & ppl), classification accuracy (MMLU-style), ROUGE-L and BLEU (detokenized), QA EM/F1, and a placeholder for task-specific scorers.

A calibration run step that executes HQP for a given quant profile and produces a signed JSON artifact with per-example metrics, aggregated deltas vs baseline, and gating recommendation (pass/fail/warn).
Integration with rollout orchestration such that a failed gate prevents automatic promotion of a quant profile and surfaces clear diagnostic links in the Console UI.
Unit and integration tests covering: tokenization parity, metric reproducibility with fixed seeds, and end-to-end gating behavior using a synthetic golden dataset.

Performance: lightweight CI scorer completes on a single standard runner for 500 examples in < 90s (wall time) and heavy validation runs scale to our distributed eval cluster with < 2x overhead compared to current harness for identical workloads.
Documented metric contract and runner config in Confluence and a sample pipeline definition that can be executed by reproducible CI and the offline calibration job scheduler.

Add tokenization cache and batched scorer executor to reduce repeated tokenization cost
Hook HQP into calibration workflow to consume profile artifacts and emit a canonical report
Create CI job template (lightweight mode) and integration test using synthetic golden set
Add Console dashboard endpoints and example per-profile visualizations (link to PR)
Measure perf on calibration cluster and tune batching/IO; add optional GPU-accelerated scorer paths where beneficial

notes: Implementation must ensure numeric determinism where possible (fixed RNG seeds, explicit float fallback paths). We will ship a 'light' scorer binary for CI (no GPU, minimal deps) and a 'full' scorer that can be run on the calibration cluster with optional Rust/CUDA extensions. Consider a future follow-up to add uncertainty-aware metrics (bootstrap CIs) and drift monitoring (EWMA) for production guardrails.
